title: The Painting with Two Labels
title_ja: 二つの説明文がある絵
fact_notes: 登場人物・出来事・観察結果は架空の教材例。実測値・実在資料を主張しない。リンクは制作台帳であり外部の実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A small art gallery invited a group of teenagers to help prepare an exhibition of works made by local artists.
sentences.ja: 小さな美術館は地元の芸術家の作品展を準備するため、十代の生徒グループに協力を求めた。

sentences.en: One painting showed a person standing beside a window with a view of a quiet street.
sentences.ja: ある絵は静かな通りが見える窓のそばに立つ人物を描いていた。

sentences.en: The students were asked to write a short description that visitors could read before looking closely at the work.
sentences.ja: 生徒は来館者が作品をじっくり見る前に読める短い説明を書くよう求められた。

sentences.en: They initially believed that describing the scene would be a simple task because everyone could see the same painting.
sentences.ja: 全員が同じ絵を見られるので、当初は場面を説明するのは簡単だと思った。

sentences.en: However, one student interpreted the figure as a lonely person waiting for someone who had not arrived.
sentences.ja: しかし一人は、人物を到着していない誰かを待つ孤独な人だと解釈した。

sentences.en: Another student imagined that the person was enjoying a peaceful moment away from the demands of everyday life.
sentences.ja: 別の生徒は、その人物が日常の要求から離れた穏やかな時間を楽しんでいると想像した。

sentences.en: Neither student could find definite evidence of the person's feelings in the painted details alone.
sentences.ja: どちらも描かれた細部だけでは人物の感情の確かな根拠を見つけられなかった。

sentences.en: The gallery director encouraged the group to distinguish descriptions of visible features from possible interpretations.
sentences.ja: 館長は目に見える特徴の説明と考えられる解釈を区別するよう促した。

sentences.en: The students therefore prepared two labels for the painting and considered how each might influence a visitor's first impression.
sentences.ja: そこで絵に二つの説明文を用意し、それぞれが最初の印象にどう影響するか考えた。

sentences.en: The first label described the colors, the position of the figure, and the objects that appeared in the picture.
sentences.ja: 一つ目は色、人物の位置、絵に現れる物を説明した。

sentences.en: The second label offered two possible readings of the scene and invited visitors to consider other explanations.
sentences.ja: 二つ目は場面の二つの解釈を提示し、別の説明も考えるよう来館者に促した。

sentences.en: They placed both labels beside the painting during a small practice exhibition for their classmates.
sentences.ja: クラスメート向けの小さな練習展示で、両方の説明文を絵のそばに置いた。

sentences.en: Some visitors preferred the factual label because they wanted an opportunity to form an independent opinion.
sentences.ja: 一部の来館者は自分自身で意見を形成したいので、事実中心の説明を好んだ。

sentences.en: Others appreciated the second label because it provided a useful starting point for thinking about the artwork.
sentences.ja: 別の来館者は作品について考える手がかりになるので、二つ目を評価した。

sentences.en: The students realized that no single approach necessarily satisfied every visitor's expectations.
sentences.ja: 一つの方法が必ずしも全来館者の期待に応えるわけではないと気づいた。

sentences.en: They revised the final display so that the interpretations were clearly separated from the description of the scene.
sentences.ja: 最終展示では解釈と場面の説明が明確に区別されるよう修正した。

sentences.en: Through this activity, the students learned that an exhibition can provide information without deciding what everyone must think.
sentences.ja: 活動を通して、展示は全員が何を思うべきか決めずに情報を提供できると学んだ。

sentences.en: A helpful label can encourage attention to particular details while leaving room for different responses.
sentences.ja: 役立つ説明文は特定の細部への注意を促しながら、異なる反応の余地も残すことができる。

sentences.en: The painting had not changed, but their understanding of the relationship between artwork and audience had become richer.
sentences.ja: 絵は変わっていないが、作品と観客の関係への理解は深まった。

sentences.en: They concluded that good explanations should open a conversation rather than close it.
sentences.ja: よい説明は対話を終わらせるのではなく始めるものだと結論づけた。

questions.prompt: What were the teenagers helping to prepare?
questions.explanation_ja: 地元作家の作品展を準備した。

options: A person standing beside a window.

questions.prompt: How did one student understand the figure?
options: As a person repairing a machine.
As an artist preparing a sculpture.
As a teacher writing a lesson.
As a lonely person waiting for someone.
questions.explanation_ja: 孤独に誰かを待っていると解釈。

questions.prompt: Why could neither interpretation be treated as certain?
options: The painting did not provide definite evidence of the figure's feelings.
The students had seen different paintings.
The director had removed all colors.
The figure was not visible in the painting.
questions.explanation_ja: 感情の確かな根拠がなかった。

questions.prompt: What did the first label focus on?
options: Only the price of the painting.
questions.explanation_ja: 色や位置など観察可能な特徴。

questions.prompt: What did the second label invite visitors to do?
questions.explanation_ja: 別の解釈も考えるよう促した。

questions.prompt: Why did some visitors prefer the factual label?
options: They wanted to develop their own opinions.
They wanted the label to make every decision.
They already knew every other visitor.
questions.explanation_ja: 自分の意見を持ちたかった。

questions.prompt: Why did the final display separate descriptions from interpretations?
options: Every visitor had to adopt the same interpretation.
Visitors could distinguish observable features from possible meanings.
The gallery no longer wanted to show the painting.
The factual information had been proved false.
questions.explanation_ja: 事実と可能な解釈を区別できるようにした。

options: All paintings have exactly one acceptable meaning.
An explanation can guide attention while allowing different interpretations.
Visitors should read only one kind of artwork.
questions.explanation_ja: 説明は多様な理解への余地を残せる。

grammar.explanation_ja: thatはdescriptionを修飾する関係代名詞。

grammar.focus: Neither student could find definite evidence
grammar.explanation_ja: neitherは二人のどちらも〜ないという意味。

grammar.focus: while leaving room for different responses
grammar.explanation_ja: while＋動名詞で別の働きを同時に示す。

discourse.role_ja: 単純と思った作業の難しさを示す。
別の来館者の意見を示す。
作品は同じでも理解が変化したこと。

paraphrases.source: The students were asked to write a short description that visitors could read before looking closely at the work.
paraphrases.rewrite: They were asked to prepare a brief text for visitors to read before examining the painting.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 作品を見る前に読む短い説明を作る。

paraphrases.source: Neither student could find definite evidence of the person's feelings in the painted details alone.
paraphrases.rewrite: Neither of the two could prove the figure's feelings from the picture alone.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 絵だけでは感情を証明できない。

paraphrases.source: The students therefore prepared two labels for the painting and considered how each might influence a visitor's first impression.
paraphrases.rewrite: They prepared two captions and thought about how each could shape a visitor's initial impression.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 説明文が印象をどう変えるか考えた。

paraphrases.source: A helpful label can encourage attention to particular details while leaving room for different responses.
paraphrases.rewrite: A useful caption can direct attention without preventing people from responding differently.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 注意を促しつつ多様な反応を認める。

cloze.explanation_ja: 感情の根拠が見つからなかった。
自分自身の意見を形成。
